overview: OpenAI unveiled new AI agents, workspace tools, and the cost‑effective GPT‑6.1 Sol model at DevDay.
AMD announced an $8.2 B acquisition of World Labs to boost its AI‑chip and robotics capabilities.
The Trump administration issued an order rebranding AI as “Super Intelligence,” signaling a political shift.

top.title: DevDay 2026 Recap
top.summary: OpenAI’s DevDay introduced persistent AI agents, a shared ChatGPT surface for human‑agent collaboration, and native experiences for its 1.2 B weekly users, aiming to expand an open AI ecosystem.

top.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
top.summary: OpenAI launched GPT‑6.1 Sol, delivering near‑Astra performance on coding, document work, and multi‑step workflows at roughly one‑fifth the cost, with lower token pricing and improved factuality.

top.title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
top.summary: President Trump signed an executive order mandating U.S. agencies replace “artificial intelligence” with “Super Intelligence,” a semantic change intended to reshape public perception and regulatory language.

top.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
top.summary: AMD agreed to acquire World Labs for $8.2 B, bringing world‑model technology and research talent into its portfolio to compete with Nvidia in AI‑driven robotics and simulation.

top.title: OpenAI takes on Microsoft with the launch of what feels a whole lot like ChatGPT’s own office suite
top.summary: OpenAI announced “Space,” “Pages,” and upcoming “Slides,” AI‑enhanced collaborative office tools within ChatGPT, positioning itself directly against Microsoft’s productivity suite.

top.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
top.summary: OpenAI released “Dots,” always‑on AI assistants powered by GPT‑6 Astra, capable of interacting with 4,000+ apps, learning user preferences, and operating within ChatGPT’s new collaborative workspace.
